title: Designing for Multi-sensory Experiences in the Built Environment
research_question: What type of experiences should be designed for the built environment? How can multi-sensory design provide a systematic approach to design for experiences?

participants.description: 22 Master level university students (interaction design students) doing an excursion in Finland, sensitive towards design, moderately heterogeneous (mostly European and Asian people), digital natives. A subset of 5 university students participated in a usability test.
participants.recruitment: Participants were students doing an excursion in Finland; specific recruitment method not detailed.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Built environment during a week-long journey (e.g., airport, train) and a museum visit, including elevator contexts. Participants were asked to capture sensory experiences (positive, negative, unremarkable emotions).
An elevator ride in a museum, followed by a questionnaire about first impressions and evoked emotions.
An elevator with a new media panel UI prototype in company facilities. Some participants were blindfolded to assess the effect of music on the elevator experience.

measures.construct: Sensory experiences and evoked emotions in the built environment
measures.instrument: WhatsApp design probe (text, photo, video, audio responses to guiding questions)

measures.construct: First impressions and emotional adjectives related to elevator experience
measures.instrument: Paper questionnaire (Likert-scale adjective pairs, open-ended questions)

measures.construct: User behavior and interaction with elevator UI, and emotional response to music in elevator
measures.instrument: Usability test observation (recorded with action cameras), self-report (for blindfolded music experience)

findings.antecedent: First impression of a product, space, or service
findings.quote: The first impression of a product, space, or service is multi-sensory.

findings.consequent: sensed mainly through visual or auditory perception, but also through olfactory and haptic perception
findings.quote: the first impression was mainly sensed through visual or auditory perception, but also through olfactory and haptic perception.

findings.antecedent: Surface materials, lighting, colors, and cleanliness of the elevator
findings.quote: The influential factors were, for example, surface materials, lighting, colors, and cleanliness of the elevator.

findings.antecedent: Artificial sounds (elevator's arrival sound, button sounds, beeping sounds, music)
findings.quote: Artificial sounds, such as the elevator's arrival sound, button sounds, beeping sounds, and the music was affecting to the first impression.

findings.antecedent: Environmental sounds (elevator cage's and shaft's sounds)
findings.quote: Environmental sounds, such as the elevator cage's and shaft's sounds were noted and analyzed to evaluate the overall quality.
Haptic impressions evoked from the breeze and pushing the buttons.

findings.antecedent: Olfactory impressions (smells of other people, food, petrol fuel)
findings.quote: Olfactory impressions related to smells of other people, food, or petrol fuel, for instance. Olfactory impressions seemed to be the most difficult ones to control...

findings.antecedent: First impression of the museum elevator
findings.quote: the first impression of the elevator was positive, and people seemed to enjoy the experience a lot, which was considered mainly as something new and fascinating.
